name: EAGLE-3 throughput improvement in SGLang at batch size 64
methodology: SGLang framework, batch size 64. EAGLE-3 with draft tree depth 8. Throughput improvement 1.38x over baseline.
notes:
This is a THROUGHPUT measurement at moderate batch size, not a latency measurement at batch 1. The 1.38x at batch 64 should be compared to EAGLE-2's 3-6.5x at batch 1 - the dramatic difference illustrates the batch dilution problem. EAGLE-3 achieves up to 6.5x speedup at batch 1.

UNIT/METRIC DIRECTION CORRECTION 2026-10-04 (benchmark throughput + latency audit). The stored value is UNCHANGED; what was wrong is the `metric` enum, which labelled this record as a raw tokens/s measurement when the number is a dimensionless RATIO. Stored value is 1.38 with unit `speedup_ratio`: 1.38x the BASELINE throughput at batch size 64, not 1.38 output tokens/s. The record names its own baseline, and the number is a correct ratio of two throughputs - only its `metric` key misfiles it. This is the error docs/07-benchmarking-methodology.md section 8 warns about from the other side: a reader filtering data/benchmarks/ by `metric: decode_tok_s` expects tokens per second, so a speedup_ratio filed under that key is not a wrong number, it is a number of the wrong KIND in the one field a capacity planner is most likely to filter on. CORRECT ENUM MEMBER: none of decode_tok_s / prefill_tok_s / tps_aggregate / tok_s_per_user describes a ratio, and schemas/benchmark.schema.json is out of scope for this audit so the record is left with an explicit `unit` and this note rather than silently reclassified. Anyone selecting benchmarks by metric MUST additionally check `unit` until a speedup_ratio member exists in the enum.
